question.text: Will plant-based meat and seafood reach 10% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales before 2031?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, for any year before 2031, plant-based meat and seafood’s dollar share in the United States is greater than or equal to 10.0% of total retail packaged meat dollar sales, as reported by the [Good Food Institute](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/) (GFI).
question.fine_print:
Note that this question resolves based on share of the total retail packaged meat market and not the total meat category.

If the resolution source should have material issues such as failing to update in a timely manner, then Metaculus may name an alternative [credible source](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), as long as it judges the methodology to be substantially equivalent.

*Given the Animal Futures Tournament timeframe, scores from this question will not be included in the tournament leaderboard. However participants are required to predict on at least two of the three long-term questions, as per the tournament rules.*

research:
Plant-based meat is far from the 10% threshold, and its share has been falling. GFI's latest figure is 1.4% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales for 2025, so the share would have to grow about sevenfold. Nothing has happened that settles the question either way.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026 (page undated; data runs through 2025-11-30): GFI's resolution page gives plant-based meat and seafood a **1.4% dollar share of total retail packaged meat** for 2025. The same page puts it at about 0.7% of the total meat category, which includes random-weight meat. Plant-based dollar sales fell 10% to about $1.0B and unit sales fell 11%. Conventional meat grew 5% in dollars. The data comes from SPINS. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)
- The same page describes the 2024 share only as "less than two percent", with no exact number. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)
- The page has no explicit "last updated" date. The next annual update, covering 2026, will most likely come out around March to April 2027, going by past timing.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. The latest value of 1.4% would need roughly a 7x increase in share to reach 10.0%.
- The share has been falling, not rising: about 2% (2019) → 2.7% (2020, the peak) → under 2% (2024) → 1.4% (2025).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Beyond Meat's Q3 2026 net revenues were $64.5M, down 8.1% year over year. US retail revenues were $24.8M, down 13.2%, with volume down 20.8%. The company cites "overall weak category demand" and fewer distribution points. Some news reports say $68.8M, but the SEC filing says $64.5M. [SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001655210/000165521026000071/ex991pressrelease-q32026ea.htm)
- 2026-08: Circana/210 Analytics data for August 2026 shows refrigerated plant-based meat dollar sales of about $22.7M, down 10.2% year over year, with pounds down 13.5%. Frozen was about $61.4M, down roughly 7.8%. Stores carried an average of 8 to 9 refrigerated items, 10.4% fewer than a year earlier. These are approximate because the PDF text was partly garbled. [Circana/PBFA PDF](https://assets.noviams.com/novi-file-uploads/pbfa/resources-toolkits/August_2026_210Analytics_Circana_meat_alternatives.pdf)
- 2026-05-19: A Food Trade News article reports shrinking refrigerated shelf sets and price premiums of 30% or more over conventional meat. It says Beyond Meat stock trades under $1. [Food Trade News](https://foodtradenews.com/2026/05/19/why-plant-based-meats-future-never-arrived/)
- 2026-11-04: A ResearchAndMarkets report projects the global plant-based food market growing at a 10.6% CAGR to 2036. This is a vendor forecast covering all plant-based foods worldwide, so it is not relevant to this US metric. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/04/3395399/28124/en/plant-based-food-market-size-share-trends-global-forecast-to-2036-market-to-reach-93-95-billion-at-10-6-cagr-driven-by-flexitarian-demand-and-asia-pacific-expansion-beyond-meat-imp.html)
- I could not find a full-year 2026 total from SPINS or GFI.

## 4. Base rates
- 2019 data: about 2% of packaged meat. [GFI/PBFA via Supermarket News](https://www.supermarketnews.com/fresh-food/plant-based-food-sales-reach-5-billion)
- 2021-04-06: GFI reported 2.7% of packaged meat for 2020, the all-time high, with sales about $1.4B, up roughly 45%. [GFI press](https://gfi.org/press/plant-based-food-retail-sales-grow-27-percent-to-reach-7-billion-in-2020/)
- 2022: GFI put plant-based meat at 1.3% of total retail meat, but 15% of packaged meat in the natural channel. [Nosh](https://www.nosh.com/news/2023/gfi-plant-based-seafood-sales-outpace-total-plant-based-meat-sales)
- Dollar sales, from the question background: $682M (2017) → $1.4B (2020) → $1.43B (2022) → $1.04B (2025). The best stretch was 2017 to 2020, when sales roughly doubled in three years and share rose by about 0.7 points.
- Rough arithmetic: if the denominator, about $70-75B in packaged meat implied by the 2025 figures, stays flat, 10% would require about $7B or more in plant-based sales. That is roughly 7x the 2025 level, reached within about five years (2026-2030 data). It would take more than 45% compound annual growth each year, while conventional meat dollars are also growing (+5% in 2025).
- No year on record has seen share rise by more than about 0.7 points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Metaculus, Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market that matches this question exactly. The Kalshi prices supplied with the question (AI market share, GDP, retail sales) are unrelated.
- Metaculus, "Will alternative protein have a market share above 25% of that of meat before 2035?": about 4% community prediction when the page was captured. [Metaculus](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/8867/)
- Manifold has a market on fake meat reaching 10% or more of the US meat market by 2035. A search snippet showed 73%, but I could not verify it and it looks unreliable. Another Manifold market about 20% share growth has already resolved Yes on old GFI data and is not relevant. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Manifold/plantbased-meat-market-share-will-i)
- Expert view: GFI itself describes 2025 as the second straight year of decline and cites price, taste and shrinking shelf space. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)

## 6. Upcoming events
- Around March to April each year, 2027 through 2030: GFI/SPINS annual reports covering 2026 through 2029. The 2030 data would probably not be published before the question resolves on 2031-01-01, so in practice the last qualifying data year is likely 2029.
- Quarterly results from Beyond Meat (next around early 2027 for Q4 2026) and monthly Circana/210 Analytics reports, which give early signals.
- Things that could move the numbers:
  - reaching price parity
  - cultivated meat or blended meat-plant products (it is unclear whether GFI would count these in this metric)
  - shocks to the price of animal meat
  - shelf resets at retailers
  - GFI changing its methodology or its definition of the denominator

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05 (fetched): The GFI page says plant-based meat and seafood made up **1.4% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales in 2025**. That is about 0.7% of the whole meat category once random-weight meat is included. US retail sales were about $1.0B, with dollars down 10% and units down 11% from 2024. The data is SPINS for the 52 weeks ending 2025-11-30. Household penetration was 11%, and 62% of buyers bought more than once. [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)
- The page has no year-by-year share table. For 2024 it says only "less than two percent." [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/)
- GFI usually publishes the next annual update (2026 data) around the spring of the following year, so expect it around spring 2027. This is based on past timing, not a confirmed date.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question, but the gap is huge. At 1.4% share, reaching 10% would take roughly 7x sales with total packaged meat flat, about $7B+ against about $1.0B now. Sales are shrinking about 7-12% a year.
- The highest share I could find in GFI-linked data is about 2.5% in 2022 ([Food Dive](https://www.fooddive.com/news/plant-based-protein-tracker/564886/)). GFI's methodology may have changed between reports, so shares from different years may not compare exactly.
- The only place the share comes close to 10% is the natural-foods channel, where it was about 15% in 2022. That is not the total-market measure that decides this question. [Food Dive](https://www.fooddive.com/news/plant-based-protein-tracker/564886/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Beyond Meat Q3 2026 results:
  - US retail revenue fell 13.2% year over year to $24.8M, and US retail volume fell 20.8%.
  - Total revenue fell 8.1% to $64.5M.
  - Q4 guidance is $54-59M. [Beyond Meat IR](https://investors.beyondmeat.com/news-releases/news-release-details/beyond-meatr-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results), [SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001655210/000165521026000071/ex991pressrelease-q32026ea.htm)
- 2026-11-04: ResearchAndMarkets forecasts the global plant-based food market growing at a 10.6% CAGR to 2036. This is a generic vendor report covering all plant-based food, not US meat share. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/04/3395399/28124/en/plant-based-food-market-size-share-trends-global-forecast-to-2036-market-to-reach-93-95-billion-at-10-6-cagr-driven-by-flexitarian-demand-and-asia-pacific-expansion-beyond-meat-imp.html)
- 2025: SPINS reported US plant-based meat sales down 7.5% to $1.13B for the 52 weeks to 2025-04-20, with refrigerated burgers down 26%. Retailers cutting shelf space is cited as one cause. [AgFunder](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-by-numbers-grim-reading-for-the-us-retail-market-brighter-spots-in-foodservice-and-globally), [PLMA](https://plma.com/article/plant-based-meat-alternatives-continue-decline-sales)
- I found no 2026 SPINS or GFI total-category figures. Nothing in my searches covered Impossible Foods' 2026 performance.

## 4. Base rates
- Dollar sales (from the question background):
  - 2017 to 2020: rose from $682M to $1.4B, including +46% in 2020.
  - 2020 to 2022: flat.
  - 2023: -12%. 2024: -7%. 2025: -11%.
- Share trend: about 2.5% (2022), under 2% (2024), 1.4% (2025).
- Even the best stretch, 2017 to 2020, only about doubled sales in three years. Reaching 10% by 2030 would take sustained growth of about 50%+ a year from 2026, and that is before any recovery from the current decline. No year since 2017 has come close to that pace except the pandemic year 2020 (+46%).
- I found no example of a US alternative-protein category recovering from a multi-year decline to gain share at that scale.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction-market prices in the brief match this question. The Kalshi markets listed are about AI chatbot market share, GDP and retail sales, and none are relevant.
- I did not find a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on plant-based meat share. I did not get a Metaculus community forecast for this question.
- The only related analysis I found is The Unjournal's "Pivotal Questions" dashboard on plant-based meat share. It is unpublished and not peer reviewed, and it also cites 1.4% for 2025. [Unjournal](https://uj-pba-workshop.netlify.app/context/pb_meat_share_dashboard_claude)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2027-04: GFI's 2026 sales update. Based on Beyond Meat's US retail trend, a further decline seems likely.
- Annual GFI updates in 2028, 2029 and 2030 would cover 2027, 2028 and 2029. Data for 2030 would probably not be published before the 2031-01-01 resolution date, so 2029 is likely the last year that can count in practice.
- Possible upside factors:
  - Price parity breakthroughs.
  - Growth in whole-cut and health-positioned products (GFI notes whole-cut unit sales up 8%).
  - Large meat price inflation (for example beef), which would raise the denominator. Note that rising meat prices would also make plant-based relatively cheaper.
  - Retailers reversing shelf-space cuts.
- Downside factors: continued loss of distribution, financial distress at Beyond Meat and similar brands, and any state or federal labeling restrictions.

Sources: [GFI](https://gfi.org/resource/analyzing-plant-based-meat-and-seafood-sales/), [Food Dive](https://www.fooddive.com/news/plant-based-protein-tracker/564886/), [Beyond Meat IR](https://investors.beyondmeat.com/news-releases/news-release-details/beyond-meatr-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results), [SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001655210/000165521026000071/ex991pressrelease-q32026ea.htm), [AgFunder](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-meat-by-numbers-grim-reading-for-the-us-retail-market-brighter-spots-in-foodservice-and-globally), [AgFunder 2024](https://agfundernews.com/plant-based-by-numbers-usa-continued-declines-for-alt-meat-more-positive-news-for-alt-dairy-gfi), [PLMA](https://plma.com/article/plant-based-meat-alternatives-continue-decline-sales), [Unjournal](https://uj-pba-workshop.netlify.app/context/pb_meat_share_dashboard_claude), [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/04/3395399/28124/en/plant-based-food-market-size-share-trends-global-forecast-to-2036-market-to-reach-93-95-billion-at-10-6-cagr-driven-by-flexitarian-demand-and-asia-pacific-expansion-beyond-meat-imp.html)

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About 4 years remain. GFI publishes annual data each spring, so the 2026 through 2029 data years, and possibly 2030 if released early, can count. Yes requires GFI to report that plant-based meat and seafood made up at least 10.0% of US retail packaged meat dollar sales in some year.

**(b) Status quo.** The share is 1.4% in 2025 and falling: 2.7% in 2020, under 2% in 2024, 1.4% in 2025. Partial 2026 data shows further declines. The status quo outcome is a clear No.

**(c) Base rate.** I could not find a case of a mature US consumer food category, already in multi-year decline, growing its share about 7x in roughly 4 years. The largest one-year share gain on record was about +0.7 points, during the pandemic boom in 2020. Even repeating that every year from 2026 to 2029 would reach only about 4%. The base rate is well under 1%.

**(d) Evidence.**
- For Yes, all of it weak:
  - GFI notes health-positioned products and whole cuts showing growth in 2025, with whole-cut unit sales up 8%.
  - The natural channel share was about 15% in 2022, but that is a different metric.
- For No, all of it strong:
  - GFI's 2025 figure is a 1.4% share, with dollar sales down 10% and conventional meat up 5%.
  - Circana's August 2026 data shows refrigerated sales down 10.2% and frozen down about 7.8%, with fewer items on shelves.
  - Beyond Meat's Q3 2026 results (Nov 4, 2026) show US retail revenue down 13.2% and volume down 20.8%, which the company blames on weak category demand.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: The decline continues or levels off at 1 to 2% share through 2029. This is almost certain.
- Yes: GFI redefines the metric, for example by folding in cultivated or blended products or narrowing the denominator, and a measure it calls the same reaches 10%. Alternatively, price parity plus a severe animal meat supply shock causes an unprecedented boom. Both are very implausible.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** I start under 1%. Reaching 10% would take more than 7x growth, roughly 60% or more compound annual growth while the category is shrinking, and no organic path makes that realistic. I add a small allowance for methodology or definition changes and for resolution quirks. I make no further upward adjustment, because no market covers the same question and no evidence points toward Yes.

Probability: 1%

(a) **Time left and what Yes requires.** Roughly 4 years remain, since the question closes at the end of 2030. In practice the last qualifying data are likely GFI's 2029 figures, published around spring 2030, and possibly 2030 data if GFI publishes early. For Yes, GFI must report plant-based meat and seafood at 10.0% or more of total US retail packaged meat dollar sales for some year.

(b) **Status quo.** The latest share is 1.4% for 2025, and it has fallen every year since the 2.7% peak in 2020. The 2026 signals are also negative:
- Circana data show refrigerated sales down 10% year over year and frozen down 8%.
- Beyond Meat's US retail revenue is down 13%, with volume down 21%.

If nothing changes, the share stays around 1-1.5% and the question resolves No.

(c) **Base rate.** The reference class is mature consumer food subcategories that grew their share sevenfold within about 4 years, starting from a declining trend. That almost never happens, so the base rate is under 1%. Even at the hype peak from 2017 to 2020, share rose only about 0.7 points in three years. Reaching 10% would need about 8.6 points.

(d) **Strongest evidence.**
- For No:
  - GFI reports 1.4% share for 2025, with dollar sales down 10% and units down 11%.
  - Conventional meat dollars grew 5% in 2025, so the denominator is expanding.
  - Beyond Meat reported Q3 2026 US retail down 13.2% on 2026-11-04.
  - Circana reported shelf counts down about 10% in August 2026.
  - The price premium was 30% or more as of May 2026.
- For Yes:
  - Whole-cut alternatives grew 8% in units.
  - Health-positioned products are growing.
  - GFI notes plant-based reached 15% of packaged meat in the natural channel. This only matters if the methodology or channel definition changed, which is very unlikely.

(e) **Scenarios.**
